USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the July 6 List 1 tariffs in place and let the List 2 / List 3 comment processes run on their published calendars, but do not implement the proposed $200 billion List 3 duties now. Reopen high-level talks immediately and insist on verifiable IP / tech-transfer remedies rather than another purchase-only truce. Use the roughly seven weeks before the List 3 process closes as a negotiating window, and prepare farm-income support if talks slip past harvest.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is modest, not existential. The Section 301 record (March 22 report; June 15 List 1 targeting Made in China 2025 sectors) is a real US interest, and US macro is still healthy: industrial production is up, Michigan sentiment is 97.9, VIX is 12.29, and there is no recession signal in rates or credit. That keeps the reading well below the +0.5 “material GDP drag” anchor. The threat is above zero because China has already matched the $34 billion action (July 6) and aimed it at soybeans, autos, and aircraft; USDA has cut the US soybean-export outlook by about 11 percent, futures are down on the order of 14–20 percent, net sales to China have turned negative, and farm-belt politics (Grassley, Durbin) are already live. CNY has weakened from ~6.33 to 6.77, blunting some tariff leverage, while US goods imports from China have been front-loaded higher into July—so the bilateral deficit is not shrinking. Action should stay near zero because further immediate escalation would likely push China into non-tariff retaliation it cannot match dollar-for-dollar, hit US consumer goods on List 3, and deepen farm losses before the September–November harvest, while a rollback would abandon a live 301 case after the May 19 purchase truce already collapsed on May 29. Formal talks have stalled with no restart scheduled; the correct stance is to re-engage without new concessions, keeping List 3 as unused leverage through the August 30 comment close.
key_factors: List 1 $34B tariffs and matching Chinese retaliation already in force since July 6
Proposed List 3 $200B/10% still in comment process through late August — unused leverage
Farm-belt hit: soybean prices down ~14-20%, USDA cut US export forecast ~11%, China sales cancellations
US real economy not yet damaged: IP up, sentiment still high, VIX ~12.3
CNY depreciation (~6.8%) offsetting some tariff bite; US imports from China front-loaded higher
May 19 purchase-only truce collapsed; high-level talks stalled as of mid-July
ZTE denial-order leverage already spent in June settlement without structural IP concessions

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
List 1 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods. China imposes matching ~$34B retaliation the same day.
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff (~6,000 product lines). Public comment / hearing process begins.
University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment latest 97.9 (2018-07-01), only a modest decline; no collapse in household confidence.
US industrial production 103.36 (2018-07-01), up ~1.6% over the window — dispute not yet biting broad output.
VIX 12.29 on 2018-07-25 — equity vol is calm, not pricing a crisis.
CNY/USD 6.7658 on 2018-07-25 vs ~6.33 in late January (~6.8% yuan depreciation), offsetting part of the US tariff wedge.
US goods imports from China rose to $47.0B in July 2018 from $39.0B in February — front-loading, not a collapse in bilateral trade.
US goods exports to China $10.15B in July 2018, down from $12.65B in March — export channel already softening.

USDA cut China soy import forecast 103m to 95m tonnes and US soy exports nearly 11% (62.3m to 55.5m tonnes); soybean futures at levels where many US farmers lose money without aid; value of soybeans down ~20% since the trade war started.
High-level talks have ground to a halt with no immediate plan to restart; about seven weeks until the $200B consultation process ends after Aug 30; China called the list totally unacceptable.
Soybeans ~60% of US ag exports to China; most-active CBOT soy futures sank 14% in June; University of Tennessee study forecast at least $4.5B drop in US shipments from a 25% duty.

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the July 6 matching tariffs in place and do not fire a new unilateral tariff round before USTR finishes the List 3 comment process. Reopen a quiet channel aimed at a purchases-for-pause track (ag, energy, aircraft) without conceding industrial-policy or IP structure, and keep the WTO case and Asian soy-diversification measures running. Further tariff escalation now would give Washington the June 18 pretext to impose the $200B list; unilateral rollback would reward the May 29 collapse of the only truce that briefly worked.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not existential. The US has already put 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods aimed at aerospace, ICT, robotics and machinery (2018-07-06), and on 2018-07-10 published a proposed 10% list on ~$200B / ~6,000 lines that would hit a much larger share of our US-bound exports. The April ZTE denial order showed Washington can threaten a national champion's viability via export controls even if the ban was lifted on 2018-07-13 after a $1B fine and compliance monitors. FX is the clearest stress signal: CNY moved from about 6.33 in late January to 6.77 on 2018-07-25 (~7%), prompting a 3 July PBOC pledge not to weaponize the yuan, while Trump publicly said the yuan was "dropping like a rock." That sits near the +0.5 CHN anchor (major export sectors hit, FX pressure, firm-level targeting) but below it because List 3 is still only proposed, industrial production is still +6.0% YoY, reserves are stable near $3.14T, CPI is tame, and US goods imports from China were still rising into July (front-loading, not a collapse). Action should stay near hold/negotiate: China cannot dollar-match $200B (US goods exports to China are only ~$10B/month), and June 18 already tied a $200B hike to further Chinese retaliation. The May 19 joint statement (purchases up; Mnuchin "on hold") is the only sequence that paused US action, and it died when the White House proceeded on May 29 — so do not pre-concede structure, but do test whether a limited purchase package can again buy time while we diversify feed imports and harden tech supply chains.
key_factors: Live $34B/25% tariffs on MIC2025-linked sectors plus proposed $200B List 3 still in comment period
Severe tariff-capacity asymmetry: China cannot match $200B given ~$10B/month of US goods exports to China
CNY depreciation of ~7% since January and PBOC verbal intervention (financial-stability risk, not yet a reserve crisis)
ZTE near-death then July 13 lift: export-control weapon is proven, but Trump also showed he will bargain to save a Chinese firm
May 19 purchase-truce collapsed on May 29 — talks work only if we do not pre-concede structure
Domestic real economy not breaking: IP still +6% YoY, reserves ~$3.14T, CPI stable

sources_cited.excerpt: List 1 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods. China imposes matching ~$34B retaliation the same day.
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff (~6,000 product lines).
Trump directs USTR to identify an additional ~$200B of Chinese imports for 10% tariffs if China retaliates against the $50B action.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
CNY/USD latest 6.7658 on 2018-07-25, change +0.433 (+6.8%) over the window.
China industrial production still 106.0 (same period previous year = 100) as of 2018-07-01; growth slowing but not collapsing.
China reserves ex-gold $3.137T on 2018-07-01, only -0.5% over the window.
US goods exports to mainland China $10.15B in July 2018 — China lacks enough US import volume to match a $200B tariff list.
Commerce lifted the ZTE ban after a $1B penalty, $400M escrow, leadership overhaul and 10-year US compliance monitors.
PBOC official Sun Guofeng: China will not make the yuan's exchange rate a tool to cope with trade conflicts.
Trump said the Chinese yuan "has been dropping like a rock"; yuan continued to slide after the $200B threat.
